title: Bond Question 2: Library Acquisitions

context.text: Authorized for the ballot by the New Mexico Legislature under the 2026 Capital Projects General Obligation Bond Act. No bonds are issued unless a majority of voters approve; each bond question is voted on separately.

question.text: The 2026 Capital Projects General Obligation Bond Act authorizes the issuance and sale of library acquisition bonds. Shall the state be authorized to issue general obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed nineteen million three hundred twenty-four thousand one hundred eighty-eight dollars ($19,324,188) to make capital expenditures for academic, public school, public and tribal library resource acquisitions and provide for a general property tax imposition and levy for the payment of principal of, interest on and expenses incurred in connection with the issuance of the bonds and the collection of the tax as permitted by law?

summary.text: Asks voters to authorize the state to issue general obligation bonds not to exceed $19,324,188 for academic, public school, public and tribal library resource acquisitions. Repayment of principal and interest is by a statewide property tax levy. The guide says the State Board of Finance will set the final rate and estimated cost after the election, with bonds generally issued with maturities up to eleven years, and that the amount of property tax collected depends on existing and new debt service, assessed valuation, interest rates and timing.

measure.yesMeans: Authorizes the state to issue general obligation bonds up to $19,324,188 for academic, public school, public and tribal library resource acquisitions, paid for through a statewide property tax.
measure.noMeans: Does not authorize these bonds; the projects would not be funded by this bond issue.

researchNotes: Source: the New Mexico Secretary of State's 2026 Voter Guide and ballot question text. The guide publishes no arguments for or against the bond questions and no statement of a per-household tax cost, so none are included. Ballotpedia's dollar amounts for the bond questions ($30 million, $20 million and $230 million) differ from the official ballot text used here.
